name: Instrument Coverage and Record the First Figure
summary: Coverage instrumentation scoped to the EAP surface, opt-in (never on the default `bun test` path), plus the first coverage figure this repository has ever produced. The unit recorded is a figure PLUS its scope: the loader refuses a baseline that carries no scope path list, a per-file figure with no scope attribution, an unjustified exclusion, a scope list that disagrees with its own digest, or figures that disagree with the integrity digest of the run that produced them.

worstRows.note: the single largest drag in the surface, and it is in the protocol core.

figures.honestReading: 91.93% lines / 91.02% functions over the declared EAP surface is a good figure and it was NOT obtained by drawing the scope around the well-tested parts: the scope is exactly the five paths the task named, fixed before the number was known, with zero exclusions and zero files omitted. The weak spot is graph-core/src/eap at 76.79% functions — the protocol core is the least covered part of the surface, and types.ts (55% functions) is where that sits.

scope.exclusionPolicy: None. `scope.exclusions` is empty and the loader requires a non-empty `reason` on every entry it could ever hold, so an exclusion is enumerated and justified inside the artefact that publishes the figure it flatters. Files no test loads would appear in `neverLoaded` at zero rather than being dropped — Bun emits no LF/LH denominator for a module nothing imported, so it would otherwise vanish from the ratio instead of dragging it down. There are none today; the mechanism is unit-tested against a fixture.

timing.howMeasured: Both runs timed by measure-coverage.ts itself in one invocation (`--with-uninstrumented`) on the same machine, back to back. Not hand-entered: `timing` is inside the integrity digest, so a cheapened cost does not load.
timing.corroboration: Independent manual runs before the script existed: plain 80993 ms, instrumented 82523 ms — delta 1530 ms, same magnitude.
timing.conclusion: Instrumentation costs ~1.5s on an ~81s suite. Cheap enough for task 15 to put on the blocking path.

acceptance.statement: Line AND function figures for an explicitly enumerated path list covering all five named surfaces.
acceptance.evidence: docs/verification/coverage-baseline.json carries per-file, per-scope-path and aggregate line and function counts for all 24 files across all five declared paths. `bun scripts/verification/measure-coverage.ts --check` prints them with the scope beside them and exits 0.

acceptance.statement: A baseline entry lacking the path list is REJECTED by the loader — the figure is unusable without its scope, structurally.
acceptance.how: `loadCoverageBaseline` is the only door into a recorded figure. It throws on: absent `scope`; absent or empty `scope.paths`; a scope path entry with no kind or no reason; absent `scope.exclusions`; an exclusion with no `reason`; a per-file figure with no `scopePath`; a `scopePath` the recorded scope does not declare; `scope.sha256` disagreeing with the scope declaration; `integrity.sha256` disagreeing with the figures. There is no code path that reads the percentage without loading the document, and the document does not load without its scope.

mutationTest.against: the COMMITTED docs/verification/coverage-baseline.json, driven through the real loader

results.mutation: drop packages/mcp-server/src/tools/eap.ts from the scope list
hand-edit the aggregate line pct to 99.9
raise a per-file covered count on a file that was NOT fully covered
add an exclusion with no justification

mutationTest.falseAlarmsCorrected: Two mutations initially reported ACCEPTED and were both defects in the MUTATION, not the loader: setting `covered = total` on a file already at 100%, and emptying an already-empty `neverLoaded`. Re-run with effective mutations (a partially covered file; an added entry) — both REJECTED. Reported here because a mutation test that scores its own no-ops as passes is worse than none.
mutationTest.unitCoverage: The same rejections are pinned as unit tests in scripts/verification/measure-coverage.test.ts (25 tests). The three integrity-scope tests were verified RED by temporarily narrowing INTEGRITY_COVERS to omit `timing`, `files` and `neverLoaded`: 3 fail / 22 pass; restored: 25 pass.

acceptance.statement: Instrumented run time is measured and reported.
acceptance.evidence: timing block above; recorded in the baseline, inside the integrity digest, printed by every report.

judgementCalls.call: Where the enumerated path list lives
judgementCalls.decision: In the SCRIPT (`COVERAGE_SCOPE`), copied into the baseline with a digest over it.
judgementCalls.why: bunfig.toml was rejected: a TOML key is not loadable by the checker and can reject nothing, so acceptance 2 could not be structurally enforced there. The baseline alone was rejected: a datum must not be able to redefine what it is a datum about. The copy-plus-digest gives the baseline a self-contained, readable scope (so the figure is never quoted bare) while making a quiet edit of that copy a load failure.

judgementCalls.call: Files inside the scope that no test touches
judgementCalls.decision: Named in `neverLoaded`, never excluded, and inside the integrity digest.
judgementCalls.why: Bun's lcov emits no record at all for a module nothing imported, so such a file does not drag the ratio down — it disappears from it. Naming it is the only honest treatment. There are zero today; the path is unit-tested with a fixture so the first one that appears is visible rather than silently absent.

judgementCalls.decision: Per FILE, rolled up per scope path, plus the aggregate.
judgementCalls.why: Task 15 must report a delta a human can act on. `recall.ts fell 12 lines` is actionable; `coverage dropped 0.3%` is not. Per-file source sha256 also lets a ratchet distinguish 'coverage fell' from 'the file changed'.

judgementCalls.call: Whether to enable coverage in bunfig
judgementCalls.decision: NO. Only reporter/dir/skip-test-files keys, all inert until --coverage is passed.
judgementCalls.why: Enabling it globally would tax every developer's `bun test` for a figure only the verification scripts consume. Cost measured anyway (+1.85%) so task 15 can decide with numbers.

judgementCalls.decision: FAILS on scope-inventory drift (a scoped file appeared or vanished); WARNS on staleness (a scoped file's sha256 moved).
judgementCalls.why: A gate that failed on every source edit until someone re-ran an 82s instrumented suite would be switched off within a week, and a switched-off gate measures nothing. Task 15 owns the blocking policy; the seam is left open.
.gitignore already covers `.verification/`, and .gitignore is outside this task's scope. Bun's default `coverage/` would have left an untracked directory dirtying every working tree.

judgementCalls.decision: Redirect to a file descriptor, not a pipe.
judgementCalls.why: See findings: piping made the pre-existing Windows EBUSY teardown flake fire on 2 of 2 runs. A measurement harness must not change the timing of what it measures.

the seven gates, each with --check where applicable

pendingCiGates.orderingDependency: NONE — it reads only the committed baseline and the scoped source files, never the suite. It must NOT be placed after a coverage run; it is a document check.
pendingCiGates.whatItCatches: a baseline stripped of its scope, a per-file figure with no scope attribution, an unjustified exclusion, a scope list edited after the fact, a hand-edited percentage, and a scope inventory that no longer matches the files on disk.
pendingCiGates.runningList: register-scenarios --check, quarantine --check, assertion-fingerprint --check, reconcile-traceability --check, derive-status --check, conformance-report --check, quarantine-gate, measure-coverage --check

pendingCiGates.command: bun scripts/verification/measure-coverage.ts  (add --with-uninstrumented only where the cost figure is being refreshed; it doubles the wall clock)
pendingCiGates.orderingDependency: It RUNS the suite itself, so it must not be stacked on top of another full `bun test` in the same job unless ~82s is acceptable twice.
pendingCiGates.note: Task 15 owns the ratchet and ci.yml. Two facts it needs: (a) instrumentation costs +1.85% wall clock, so the blocking path can afford it; (b) measure-coverage.ts refuses to write a figure from a red suite, so the known Windows EBUSY flake BLOCKS measurement rather than corrupting it — a CI job that treats 'no figure' as 'figure unchanged' would silently stop measuring.

knownFlakes.observed: packages/mcp-server/test/reconnect-after-restart.test.ts EBUSY teardown — 2 failures in 2 spawned runs when the runner's stdout was piped to the parent process; 0 in 4 runs when redirected to a file descriptor.
knownFlakes.handling: Never masked: measure-coverage.ts exits non-zero and writes nothing when the suite is red. The fd redirection is in the harness, not in the test.

foundNotOwned.finding: Piping the test runner's stdout appears to trigger the Windows EBUSY SQLite handle-release race in reconnect-after-restart.test.ts (2/2 vs 0/4). The teardown's `rmSync(..., maxRetries: 10, retryDelay: 50)` is losing to the OS under backpressure.
foundNotOwned.owner: whoever owns that test; task 15 must not run the suite through a pipe.
foundNotOwned.severity: blocks measurement, does not corrupt it

foundNotOwned.finding: packages/graph-core/src/eap/types.ts is 55% function-covered (11/20) and 72.67% line-covered — the least-tested file in the protocol core, and the biggest single lever on the aggregate.
foundNotOwned.owner: not this task; recorded so the first ratchet target is chosen from evidence rather than taste.

foundNotOwned.finding: The suite instruments and reports on scripts/verification/*.ts and test helpers too (252 instrumented files repo-wide vs 24 in scope). Nothing was done with that: a second scope would need its own declaration and its own justification.

`bun run verify` still does not pass --reporter=junit, so derive-status --check continues to depend on a separately produced .verification/junit.xml. Unchanged by this task; already on the task 20 list.
